BOUNDARY: The proof correctly handles the extremal cases admitted by the hypotheses. If limsup < 1 then Λ is a real number in [0,1); taking t = (Λ+1)/2 gives a strict gap, and all inequalities remain strict. If liminf > 1 then the tail infimum eventually exceeds 1, so Kₖ becomes strictly negative. Sequences with qₖ → 1 from either side lie outside both hypotheses and make no claim. The extended‑real machinery is used only for existence of limsup/liminf; all quantities that appear in the inequalities are real. No counterexample to the stated implication was found (e.g., aₖ = 2⁻ᵏ satisfies limsup < 1 and yields liminf Kₖ = 1 > 0; aₖ = 2ᵏ satisfies liminf > 1 and makes Kₖ = -½ ≤ 0). The constant‑weight series ∑ 1/ζₖ = ∑ 1 diverges by the term test, and the positivity of all aₖ keeps every reciprocal well defined.
